findings.claim: getAllowedLocations computes the tag/user intersection in Java on top of getLocationsByTag, which fetches and hydrates every non-retired Location plus ceil(N/100) batched location_tag_map selects, so the per-request cost grows with the size of the location table rather than with the size of the result; the same DAO the PR edits already answers this in one SQL statement via getLocationsHavingAllTags.
findings.evidence: Measured with Hibernate SQL logging (temporarily flipped api/src/test/resources/log4j2.xml org.hibernate.SQL to DEBUG, restored afterwards) using a throwaway BaseContextSensitiveTest probe that created 250 extra non-retired untagged Locations (253 total), tagged locations 1 and 2, assigned location 2 to user 1, then flushed+cleared the session so the User was detached exactly as Context.getAuthenticatedUser() hands it to a request. Statement counts between stdout markers: getAllowedLocations(restricted user) = 9 statements -> [users+person join, person_name, person_attribute, person_address, `select ... from location` (0 binds, all 253 rows hydrated), 3x `select ... from location_tag_map` with 100 bind params each, `select ... from user_location`] for a result of size 1; getAllowedLocations(unrestricted user 501) = 12 statements; getLocationsByTag(tag) alone = 4 statements; getLocationsHavingAllTags([tag]) = 1 statement returning the same 2 tagged locations. The 3x100-bind tag batches are ceil(253/100) and follow from Location.tags carrying @BatchSize(size = 100) (api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/Location.java:145-149), so the query count is 1+ceil(N/100) and the hydrated-entity count is N, both unbounded in the location table size. Source of the fetch-all: LocationServiceImpl.getLocationsByTag (api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/impl/LocationServiceImpl.java:213-223) loops dao.getAllLocations(false) and filters on l.getTags().contains(tag) in Java; the SQL-side alternative HibernateLocationDAO.getLocationsHavingAllTags (api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/db/hibernate/HibernateLocationDAO.java:402-425) does the tag filter with a criteria subquery and the same retired=false predicate. Consumer trace: the companion PR openmrs/openmrs-module-webservices.rest#762 adds LocationForCurrentUserSearchHandler3_0.search, which calls Context.getUserService().getAllowedLocations(Context.getAuthenticatedUser(), locationTag) and wraps the result in NeedsPaging, i.e. it pages in memory after the whole table has been hydrated; per TRUNK-6669 this endpoint replaces GET /ws/rest/v1/location?tag=Login+Location in esm-login-app, so it runs on every login. Caveat checked before recommending: getAllLocations(false) sorts by name (HibernateLocationDAO.java:116) while getLocationsHavingAllTags has no orderBy, so a naive swap would silently drop the picker's name ordering - the clean fix is one DAO query joining l.tags with the optional user_location restriction and `order by l.name`, which also removes the user re-read in performance-4.

findings.claim: User.locations is a lazy @ManyToMany with no @BatchSize, so initializing it across n Users costs n separate `select ... from user_location where user_id = ?` queries; both collections on Location already carry @BatchSize(size = 100).
findings.evidence: Measured both ways in the same probe with a positive control. Probe window loaded UserService.getAllUsers() (3 users in the standard test dataset) after flush+clear and touched u.getLocations() on each: as written, 3 `select ... from user_location where user_id = ?` statements with 1 bind param each (16 statements in the window). I then temporarily added @org.hibernate.annotations.BatchSize(size = 100) to the locations field, re-ran the identical probe, and got exactly 1 user_location statement with 100 bind params (14 in the window); User.java was restored with `git checkout --` and `grep -c BatchSize api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/User.java` returns 0. Sibling precedent: Location.tags and Location.childLocations both carry @BatchSize(size = 100) (api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/Location.java:141 and :147). Named consumer: the companion PR openmrs/openmrs-module-webservices.rest#762 UserResource3_0.getRepresentationDescription adds `locations` to FullRepresentation, so GET /ws/rest/v1/user?v=full over n users pays n extra queries.

findings.claim: User.locations carries no @Cache, unlike the User entity itself and the User.roles collection three lines above, so the user_location row set is read from the database on every getAllowedLocations call and on every saveUser of a detached User even when locations were never touched.
findings.evidence: Annotation asymmetry read directly: User is @Cacheable + @Cache(usage = CacheConcurrencyStrategy.READ_WRITE) (api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/User.java:66-67) and User.roles carries its own @Cache(usage = CacheConcurrencyStrategy.READ_WRITE) (line 97); the new locations collection (lines 108-111) carries neither. Second-level caching is on by default: api/src/main/resources/hibernate.default.properties sets hibernate.cache.use_second_level_cache=true and hibernate.cache.region.factory_class=infinispan, and api/src/main/resources/infinispan-api.xml already declares the default `entity` region, so no config file would need changing. Measured cost: in my SQL-logged probe a cold-session getAllowedLocations always ended with `select ... from user_location where user_id = ?` (1 bind), and a saveUser on a detached User that never touched locations also issued that query (14 statements in the window, the last one being the user_location select) because HibernateUtil.saveOrUpdate merges the detached entity and must load the persistent collection to diff it. I did NOT measure that adding @Cache actually produces an Infinispan hit in this configuration, so the remedy's effect is asserted from the roles precedent, not measured.

findings.claim: The unconditional dao.getUser(user.getUserId()) re-read rehydrates the whole User/Person graph just to reach the user's assigned location ids, which the method is the only consumer of.
findings.evidence: In the cold-session probe (user detached via flush+clear, then getAllowedLocations called) the first four of the nine statements were the users row joined to person, then person_name, person_attribute and person_address - the Person collections follow because User.person is @ManyToOne(fetch = FetchType.EAGER) (api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/User.java:83-86). None of that graph is used: the method only reads persisted.getLocations(). HibernateUserDAO.getUser is a plain session.get(User.class, userId) (api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/db/hibernate/HibernateUserDAO.java:244-247). A DAO query for the assigned location ids, or folding the restriction into the single intersection query recommended in performance-1, removes the re-read entirely. Attribution caveat: the authenticated test user is also user 1, so I cannot fully separate these four statements from the @Authorized advice's own user access; the unrestricted-user window (a different user id, 501) showed the same one users select plus the same three person-collection selects alongside three separate role_privilege/role_role statements, which is consistent with the four being the re-read.

what_i_swept: Verified the diff stat first: `git diff 28e3bab9e206170df7fd43cf709495b6d45fe16a b7cd909d245086fa10691496f88e5ec6971b77c2 --stat` = 8 files, +216/-6, matching the brief. Read the JIRA ticket (TRUNK-6669, reachable) to establish that the new method backs the login-location picker, i.e. a per-login path, which is what makes the cost questions load-bearing rather than academic. Then swept each changed line for my dimension: (a) the new User.locations mapping - fetch type, cascade, @Independent, @BatchSize, @Cache - against its closest sibling User.roles in the same class and against both Location collections; (b) UserServiceImpl.getAllowedLocations - the re-read, the getLocationsByTag call, and the Java-side stream filter; (c) HibernateLocationDAO.deleteLocation's new native delete; (d) the liquibase changeset's PK/FK index shape (PK leads with user_id, which is the right leading column for the lazy collection load; the user_role sibling relies on FK indexes the same way); (e) the LOCATION_ID constant extraction (no runtime effect). Rather than reading off the diff I measured: I temporarily set org.hibernate.SQL to DEBUG in api/src/test/resources/log4j2.xml and ran narrow `mvn -o -pl api test -Dtest=...` selections (never `install`), first on the PR's own UserServiceTest#getAllowedLocations_shouldReturnOnlyTheAssignedLocationsThatCarryTheTag - which turned out to run in an already-warm session and so hid the cost - then on a throwaway probe that scaled the location table to 253 rows and detached the User via flush+clear to reproduce the real request shape. That produced per-call statement counts for getAllowedLocations (restricted and unrestricted), getLocationsByTag, and getLocationsHavingAllTags side by side, and a proper positive control for the @BatchSize claim (3 queries without, 1 query with). Outward trace, one level past the diff in both directions: downstream I read the companion consumer PR openmrs/openmrs-module-webservices.rest#762 (diff only, no review conversation) and confirmed LocationForCurrentUserSearchHandler3_0 calls getAllowedLocations with Context.getAuthenticatedUser() and pages the result in memory via NeedsPaging, and that UserResource3_0 exposes `locations` on FullRepresentation - the consumer that turns the missing @BatchSize into an N+1; upstream/unchanged-neighbour side I read LocationServiceImpl.getLocationsByTag and HibernateLocationDAO.getLocationsHavingAllTags (the SQL-side sibling in the same file the PR edits), RequiredDataAdvice.recursivelyHandle to confirm @Independent really does skip the field (line 306) and so avoids force-initializing the collection on every save/void/retire, HibernateUserDAO.saveUser/HibernateUtil.saveOrUpdate for the merge path, and HibernateContextDAO's login path (setLastLoginTime -> saveUserProperties) to check whether login pays the extra collection read - it does not, because the candidate user is session-resident there so saveOrUpdate short-circuits. I also checked the write side for amplification: a saveUser that never touches locations issues one extra read and no delete/insert, and a saveUser that does replaces the row set with delete-all + re-insert exactly as user_role already does, so no finding. Cleared without a finding: the stream filter is not quadratic (assigned is a PersistentSet initialized by a single query, and BaseOpenmrsObject hashCode/equals are uuid-based, so contains is O(1) per element - one user_location statement in every trace confirms no per-element proxy initialization); the liquibase changeset adds one changeset to startup; @Transactional(readOnly = true) avoids an auto-flush on the read path. Restored both mutated files with `git checkout --`, deleted the probe test, and `git status --porcelain` is empty.
out_of_scope: Test coverage: LocationServiceTest#purgeLocation_shouldDeleteLocationAssignedToAUser never issues a `delete from location` - in my SQL trace the native `delete from user_location where location_id = ?` was the last statement of the run and session.remove was never flushed, so the assertNull passes from the session alone and the test would still pass with the native delete removed; it does not exercise the FK it exists to protect.

Approach: deleteLocation special-cases user_location, but other tables still reference location with RESTRICT - my probe's purgeLocation(location 3) failed on FKDCVKCH4X1BSU32NS3YDA9MKEC: PUBLIC.PATIENT_IDENTIFIER FOREIGN KEY(LOCATION_ID), so this fixes one FK of several rather than the general purge problem.

Solution fit: the changeset creates user_location with a composite PK (user_id, location_id) rather than the user_location_id surrogate key the ticket's proposed DDL specifies (the composite is arguably better, but it diverges from the accepted ticket).

Correctness: the user_location FK on user_id is onDelete=RESTRICT, so purging a user who has assigned locations will fail in the same way purging a location did, and nothing in the diff clears the rows on that side.
Correctness: getAllowedLocations silently returns an empty list for a null tag and for a non-persisted user, rather than distinguishing 'no tag asked for' from 'nothing allowed'.

Correctness: the native delete bypasses the session cache; the author's own inline comment at HibernateLocationDAO.java:129-132 acknowledges it and states the no-caller-holds-a-loaded-User assumption, which is an unchanged-neighbour assumption someone should confirm.
could_not_verify: Whether the new createNativeQuery(...).executeUpdate() in HibernateLocationDAO.deleteLocation forces a full session flush and/or invalidates every Infinispan second-level-cache region (it synchronizes no query spaces). I ran the PR's own purge test with SQL logging, but nothing was pending at that point in the trace so the result was inconclusive, and purgeLocation is a rare admin path, so I deliberately did not build a finding on it rather than asserting the Hibernate 7.4.7 behaviour from memory.

Whether adding @Cache to User.locations would actually be served from Infinispan under the shipped configuration - performance-3's observation (uncached, one query per call, asymmetric with User.roles) is measured, but I did not run an L2-statistics comparison to prove the remedy.

Real-world location table sizes. I scaled my probe to 253 non-retired rows synthetically and derived the 1+ceil(N/100) growth from Location.tags's @BatchSize(100); I did not measure a production instance, so the absolute severity of performance-1 at a given deployment's scale is extrapolated, not observed.
notes: Two process notes for the merger. First, the brief's JDK instruction is wrong for this repo: openmrs-core's root pom sets maven.compiler.release=21, so JAVA_HOME=openlogic-openjdk-8 cannot build it. Every run here used /Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jdk-21.jdk/Contents/Home with `mvn -o -pl api test -Dtest=<narrow selection>`; `mvn install` was never invoked, and the shared ~/.m2 was not written to. Second, on disposition: none of my four findings is blocking, and that is a deliberate call rather than hedging. The expensive shape in performance-1 is inherited from the pre-existing getLocationsByTag, which already backs the endpoint this one replaces, so the PR declines an available improvement rather than introducing a regression - and the public signature getAllowedLocations(User, LocationTag) does not need to change to fix it later, which is what keeps it out of blocking territory. The strongest single fact for a reviewer to carry: 9-12 SQL statements and N hydrated Location entities per login-location request, against 1 statement from a method that already exists in the very DAO this PR edits. performance-1 and performance-4 share one fix (a single DAO query joining l.tags with the optional user_location restriction, ordered by name), so they should be resolved together; performance-2 and performance-3 are independent one-annotation changes.
